comment: Register of legal units for non-commercial organisations does not engage company law digital tools; drop RI-TEC-035, keep RI-TEC-015.
Chapter 24 item on alignment with the Temporary Protection Directive; only the right to work element fits RI-FMW-014 (compare G4-D03).
Consular staffing for e-visa files is back-office processing capacity; RI-TEC-037 is a weak fit, possibly out (R22).
A law on e-invoicing in procurement is legal alignment, not replacement of the system; RI-TEC-038 is a stretch, consider queued_unmatched.
The sentence only lists responsible bodies; MEC-08 rests on a contrast with another item, not this text.
Public sector use of a generative AI tool is not framework alignment or enforcement structures; RI-TEC-001 is a loose fit (noted).
e-Notariat concept may be a back-office notarial system (R22); in scope only if it delivers online services; already flagged.
Security audit of one register system is closer to a sector back-office matter than national operational cyber capacity; flagged.
Equipment for general digitalisation of the employment service, not stated as linked to EURES or labour mobility; RI-FMW-005 is stretched.

Non-transposition of a Blue Card Directive provision is legal alignment with Chapter 24 legal migration acquis, which G4-D03 says would stretch RI-FMW-014; should be out_of_scope (consistent with -0004, -0051, -0060 in the out-of-scope sample).
Loose fit (noted): need for further analysis of private access to state data; neither RI-TEC-017 nor RI-TEC-028 is clearly the subject.
Ministry mandate (M2): MDA-GOV-2023-001-0146 treats the same kind of sentence as country_response, this one as implementation.
Digitalising active labour market services is general PES modernisation, not stated as EURES or mobility capacity; RI-FMW-005 stretched, RI-TEC-037 alone fits better.
A view on proportional pay for foreign workers states no legal gap; MEC-01 not supported.
Cybersecurity is not named in the sentence; the RI-TEC-022 link rests on the preceding item (G4 seed kept).
